title: Airflow Task Queue Latency
dataSources: Airflow logs (`airflow:scheduler`, `airflow:worker`, `airflow:task`), REST API `/dags/*/dagRuns`, StatsD counters (`airflow:statsd`), and metadata tables via DB Connect.
app: Airflow task/scheduler logs via Universal Forwarder; Airflow REST API (`/api/v1`) and StatsD/OpenTelemetry metrics via HEC scripted inputs; Airflow metadata database (`dag_run`, `task_instance`, `job`) via Splunk DB Connect.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=airflow:task
| eval queue_latency=queued_duration
| stats avg(queue_latency) as avg_s, p95(queue_latency) as p95_s by queue
| where p95_s>120
| sort - p95_s
description: Computes how long tasks sit in the queued state before a worker picks them up, broken down by executor queue, to reveal worker-capacity shortfalls.
value: High queue latency means tasks are ready but there are not enough workers; quantifying it per queue drives right-sized autoscaling and protects SLAs.
implementation: Derive queued duration from task instance start vs. queued timestamps (logs or metadata DB); schedule hourly and alert when p95 latency crosses your window.
visualization: Table of queue by p95 latency, timechart of queue wait.
grandmaExplanation: We measure how long pipeline jobs wait for a free worker so you know when to add capacity before things run late.
